warmup.text: Someone stole Jack and Praiseworthy's money, and the thief is on the ship. Before you read, predict: how could a butler catch a thief with no proof?

words.text: Use the roots to work out new words, and put phrases where they belong. In the game, weigh six more words. One of them looks like a hear word, but it isn't.

reading.text: Read Chapter 2. At the first pause, guess how a pig could catch a thief. At the second, say when you figured out the trick, or how the book fooled you.

assignment.text: Three questions about Praiseworthy's plan and the thief. Then revise your adventure plan with the checklist, and add one thing that isn't what it seems.

do: Tap the highlighted words in the first sentence.
Fix the second sentence in the box.
Tap See the Answer to check.
how.why: A phrase that tells where or when puts the reader in the scene.

do: Read the question.
Write 2 or 3 sentences in your reading journal.
Then go on to Word Study.
how.why: Thinking before you read gives you something to watch for.

do: Read the six words.
Break each place name into syllables and mark the loud one.
Write your Gold Rush sentence in the box.
how.why: This is your Show What You Know for spelling this week.

do: Read the two new words and how the roots explain them.
Tap a word, then tap its meaning.
Match all four.
how.why: Roots let you guess a new word before you look it up.

do: Tap a word.
Tap its meaning.
Match all five.
how.why: Matching shows you know each word on its own.

do: Read the stacked phrases.
Type the word from the bank that fits each sentence.
Tap Check My Work.
how.why: Stacked phrases put the reader right in the scene.

do: Read the reading focus below.
Open your book and read Chapter 2.
Then do the Read Like a Writer box and the Virtue Watch at the end of this tab.
how.why: The pause boxes are places to stop and think while you read.

do: Read the three lenses.
Tap the one you will use today.
Keep it in mind as you read. You will use it at the end.
how.why: An adventure needs obstacles. Watching how the hero gets past one is half the fun.
how.use: You will use it in reading question 1.

do: Read today's step and the checklist.
Check your plan one item at a time and fix what is missing.
Add one thing that isn't what it seems.
how.why: A good plan makes the draft next week much easier.

a story about a robbery and a clever plan

beside: Not on it, not in it.
Across: They go from one side to the other.
inside: The nugget is hidden in something.

game.title: The Assayer's Scale
game.sub: This week's word game · 6 words today
game.look: An assayer tested gold in the Gold Rush, to tell real gold from fool's gold. Here you test words. A word with aud (hear) goes on the HEAR pan. A word with or (speak) goes on the SPEAK pan. A word that only looks like one is fool's gold.

do: Read the word on the nugget.
Think about what it means.
Tap HEAR, SPEAK, or Fool's gold.
Tap Next word.
how.why: A root only helps if it is really there. Testing the meaning keeps you from being fooled.

game.doneLine: Come back tomorrow for six more words.

nuggets.why: aud + io: sound you can hear.
Fool's gold! It comes from a Latin word for bold, not hear. Audacious means boldly daring.
nuggets.miss: It starts with aud, but does it mean hearing? Think about bold.

nuggets.why: No root here. Organ comes from a Greek word for tool.
aud + itory: having to do with hearing.
A long piece of music with singing, first sung in a prayer hall. Its root means speak or pray.

art.title: The Way They Go to California
art.alt: A black-and-white comic print: a crowded sailing ship, an air-ship and a rocket overhead, a man falling from a parachute, and a crowd on a dock waving picks and shovels.
art.look: A comic print sold in New York in 1849, the year the novel begins. The artist pokes fun at the rush: an air-ship, a rocket, a man under a parachute, and a crowd on the dock shouting that they have paid and still can't get aboard. Fleischman's novel jokes about the same rush.

virtue.name: loyalty
virtue.title: The loyalty meter
virtue.intro: Think about one moment from Chapter 2.
virtue.moment: Praiseworthy has the idea for the coal-dust trick. But he tells the captain, “Master Jack here has hit upon a scheme to expose the rascal.” Jack only got the pig dusty.
virtue.ask: How loyal is Praiseworthy to his partner here? Slide to show.
virtue.take: Mason's take: very loyal. He shares the credit so his young partner can stand tall.
